newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Further signs of EU oil stock replenishment seen.
newsitem.headline: Further signs of EU oil stock replenishment seen.

text.p: A modest draw of European Union middle distillate stocks in December did not detract from a recent trend of stock replenishment, analysts said on Monday.
Their comments followed Monday's release of oil stock figures for the European Union, excluding Sweden, in the latest monthly report from Stitchting Euroilstock.
The report showed middle distillate stocks were down a modest 370,000 barrels, or 0.1 percent, to 297.38 million barrels, leaving them 5.03 million barrels, or 1.7 percent higher year-on-year.
"Normally or quite often we'd see a bigger draw," said Geoff Pyne, energy analyst at UBS.
"This means (stocks in) December (were) approaching normal for the time of year which is quite surprising if you look just three months back," he added.

At the end of September, distillate stocks represented a year-on-year shortfall of 33.47 million barrels, but the level steadily rose in the following two months as refinery utilisation has topped 90 percent.

In November, refinery crude runs hit record levels, rising 690,000 barrels per day, or 6.3 percent, to 11.729 million barrels. The utilisation rate climbed to 93.09 percent. In December, intake slipped, but the utilisation rate has clung above the 90 percent level.
Analysts agree that this provided confirmation of a generally bearish trend for middle distillates on both sides of the Atlantic.
However, some urge caution lest the bearish sentiment got out of control. Distillate stocks were still below the level of 1994 and remained down from the average during the 1988-1995 period.
"Refinery utilisation rates have been high, but we've had very strong demand and cold weather for the last couple of weeks," said Cindy Poynter of oil consultants Bonner and Moore.
Poynter said distillate stocks were still two to three days of supply below historical levels. At the start of autumn, stocks were up to five days of supply below.
The cold weather of the past two weeks, she added, was likely to have drawn stock levels down further.
